newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hits Kabila over "small" refugee problem.
newsitem.headline: France hits Kabila over "small" refugee problem.

text.p: France, which backs ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, accused his opponent Laurent Kabila on Monday of making an intolerable statement when he reportedly said Zaire's refugee issue was "a small problem".

French media widely reported this weekend that Kabila, leader of the rebels who control half of the vast African country, said the issue of about 100,000 Rwandan refugees scattered in the Zaire jungle was a small problem.
"The international community cannot tolerate that the fate of tens of thousands of people be described as a small problem," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a briefing.

"The international community must mobilise and make Mr Kabila understand his movement must respect humanitarian precepts. The non-access for aid groups to the refugees is not satisfactory," Rummelhardt said.
Asked about allegations that refugees were massacred, Rummelhardt said: "You cannot say this time that you did not know. France is shocked by what is happening."
International agencies hope to gain access to some of the refugees after Kabila ordered their repatriation within 60 days.
Aid agencies lost track of the Rwandan Hutus after they disappeared last week from makeshift camps about 35 km (20 miles) south of Kisangani.
Kabila said his forces knew where the bulk of the refugees were and he would help U.N. officials to locate them.

Kabila denied that his forces sparked the exodus by attacking the camps and said he was seeking a personal apology from U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, who described the fate of the refugees as "slow extermination."

Some of the refugees played a prominent role in the 1994 slaughter of an estimated 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda and Kabila said last week that criminals among them had transported their lawlessness to Zaire.
More than a million Hutus fled Rwanda to escape reprisals for the genocide. Most returned in a repatriation sparked by Kabila's sweeping rebel advance through eastern Zaire.
